2608.30948.title: Detecting AI Impostors: How Do Middle Schoolers Identify LLM Agents in a Live Collaborative Setting?
2608.30948.paper_summary: LLMs can imitate how people write, which raises concerns about impersonation, trust, and detection in social settings. These concerns are especially important for adolescents, who use generative AI frequently but may struggle to recognize it. We introduce \textit{DoppelBot}, a cooperative social deduction game designed to study how young people detect and respond to AI impersonation. Through studies with middle schoolers, we investigate whether a DoppelBot prompts reflection on privacy and impersonation, how repeated exposure affects AI-detection accuracy as agents become more personalized, and which strategies students use to identify AI doppelgängers. We find that students' detection accuracy improves over time, driven by a shift from relying on linguistic cues to leveraging shared social and contextual signals. Students also demonstrated an understanding of AI limitations such as embodiment and reflected on broader issues such as data privacy. To support future research, we release an anonymized dataset of game transcripts and voting behavior.
2608.30948.paper_summary_zh: LLMs 可以模仿人們的寫作方式，這引發了在社交環境中有關冒充、信任和檢測的擔憂。這些擔憂對於青少年來說尤其重要，他們經常使用生成式 AI，但可能難以識別它。我們介紹了 \textit{DoppelBot}，這是一款合作社交推理遊戲，旨在研究年輕人如何檢測和應對 AI 冒充。通過對中學生的研究，我們調查了 DoppelBot 是否促使反思隱私和冒充，重複接觸如何影響 AI 檢測的準確性，因為代理變得更加個性化，以及學生用來識別 AI 雙胞胎的策略。我們發現學生的檢測準確性隨著時間的推移而提高，這是由於他們從依賴語言線索轉向利用共享的社交和情境信號。學生們還表現出對 AI 限制的理解，例如具身性，並反思更廣泛的問題，如數據隱私。為了支持未來的研究，我們發布了一個匿名的遊戲記錄和投票行為數據集。
